evidence: Ter. Eun. 85: accēde ad ignem hunc
Cic. Off. 1.52: patī ab igne ignem capere
terms.comment: Fire in general, and the fire one sits by or cooks on; to light one is ignem excitāre (see kindle a fire).

terms.gloss: a fire that destroys, a blaze
evidence: Traupman 167, 315: fire, incendium; put out a fire, incendium exstinguere
Publ. S 48: vīcīnum velle ulcīscī incendiō
terms.comment: A house or a forest on fire.

phrases.latin: Bonō animō es: accēde ad ignem hunc; jam calēscēs plūs satis
phrases.english: cheer up: come to this fire; you’ll soon be more than warm enough

phrases.latin: stultum est vīcīnum velle ulcīscī incendiō
phrases.english: it is foolish to take revenge on a neighbour by fire

phrases.latin: sēdulus hospes paene macrōs ārsit dum turdōs versat in ignī
phrases.english: our busy host nearly went up in flames while turning some skinny thrushes on the fire

sources: Lewis & Short: ignis · Lewis & Short: incendium · Lewis & Short: ardeo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 167, 315, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-terentius, loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-publilius, loci-horatius), checked against the editions named there.
